summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of COPD, chronic alcohol dependence, tobacco use, and prior trauma, was admitted for dyspnea, fever, and productive cough suggestive of healthcare-associated pneumonia. He had a week of fevers, chills, night sweats, and 10-pound weight loss. Initial labs showed leukocytosis and elevated lactate. A chest X-ray revealed atelectasis without overt pneumonia, but he was treated with IV antibiotics due to clinical concern. His infection markers improved, and his respiratory status stabilized. He also received diazepam for moderate alcohol withdrawal, with CIWA scores around 11, and remained at risk for delirium tremens. Despite clinical improvement, he eloped against medical advice approximately 48 hours into treatment, before blood cultures returned. He was discharged on home medications with urgent follow-up recommended.
